hello-world-for-nims-on-cks/1-prerequisi.title: Prerequisites
hello-world-for-nims-on-cks/1-prerequisi.intro: Before deploying a NVIDIA NIM on CKS, verify that you have kubectl access to a CKS cluster with GPU nodes and that your NGC credentials are configured.

sections.heading: Connect to your CKS cluster
sections.prose: Ensure you can reach the cluster and that `kubectl` is properly configured. The following command lists cluster nodes and their status.

sections.heading: Verify GPU node availability
sections.prose: NIM containers require GPU resources. Confirm that your cluster has nodes with NVIDIA GPUs available.

sections.heading: Create an NGC image-pull secret
sections.prose: NIM container images are hosted on NVIDIA NGC (nvcr.io). Create a Kubernetes `docker-registry` secret so the cluster can pull the image. Replace the `--docker-password` value with your own NGC API key.

hello-world-for-nims-on-cks/2-deploy-nim.title: Deploy the NIM
hello-world-for-nims-on-cks/2-deploy-nim.intro: Deploy a NVIDIA NIM as a Kubernetes Deployment backed by a ClusterIP Service. The NIM container downloads the model on first start and exposes an OpenAI-compatible API on port 8000.

sections.heading: Create the NGC API key secret
sections.prose: The NIM runtime reads the NGC API key from an environment variable sourced from a Kubernetes secret. This is separate from the image-pull secret created earlier.

sections.heading: Apply the NIM manifest
sections.prose:
The manifest below creates a single-replica Deployment with one GPU, health probes, and a ClusterIP Service. The `imagePullSecrets` field references the NGC credentials created in the previous step.

Key resource settings:
- `nvidia.com/gpu: 1` — requests one GPU from the CKS scheduler
- Readiness and liveness probes hit the NIM's built-in `/v1/health/ready` and `/v1/health/live` endpoints
- The Service exposes port 8000 for in-cluster access
- An `emptyDir` volume is mounted at `/opt/nim/.cache` for model weight caching

sections.heading: Wait for the NIM to become ready
sections.prose: On first start the NIM container downloads the model weights, which may take several minutes depending on model size. The readiness probe will report `True` once the model is loaded and the inference server is accepting requests.

hello-world-for-nims-on-cks/3-query-nim.title: Query the NIM
hello-world-for-nims-on-cks/3-query-nim.intro: Once the NIM is ready, you can send inference requests using the OpenAI-compatible `/v1/chat/completions` endpoint. This works from any pod in the cluster via the Service DNS name.

sections.heading: Send a chat completion request
sections.prose: Use `curl` to send a JSON payload to the NIM. The request format is identical to the OpenAI Chat Completions API, making it easy to swap in any NIM model.

sections.heading: Query via in-cluster Service DNS
sections.prose: From any pod in the same cluster, you can reach the NIM using its Kubernetes Service DNS name: `<service-name>.<namespace>.svc.cluster.local:8000`. This is the recommended pattern for production workloads.

hello-world-for-nims-on-cks/4-cleanup.title: Clean up
hello-world-for-nims-on-cks/4-cleanup.intro: Remove the NIM deployment, service, and secrets to free GPU resources. Always clean up when you are done experimenting — GPU nodes are a shared resource.

sections.heading: Delete all resources
sections.prose: The following commands remove the Deployment, Service, and both secrets created during this tutorial.
